section_summary: This section concludes the monograph’s survey of Japanese residents and activities in Colombia, then covers Venezuela and Ecuador before presenting an extensive account of Peru and beginning the chapter on Bolivia. It describes Japanese commercial networks, migration and settlement, propaganda, suspected espionage and Axis collaboration, together with wartime surveillance, internment, deportation and property controls. Maps, population and trade tables, photographs and occupational statistics supplement the narrative.

subfiles.title: Japanese Monograph—Latin America (continued)
subfiles.about: Continuation of a country-by-country intelligence survey of Japanese population, commerce, political influence, propaganda, espionage and wartime controls in Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador, Peru and Bolivia.
subfiles.summary: The report finishes its treatment of Colombia with profiles of suspected Japanese leaders, commercial representatives and diplomatic personnel, followed by Colombian surveillance and internment measures. It then surveys the small Japanese communities of Venezuela and Ecuador, emphasizing commercial activity, propaganda, suspected strategic surveys and government restrictions. The much larger Peru chapter supplies migration, population, occupational and trade statistics; describes Japanese institutions and businesses; and assesses allegations of espionage alongside deportations, asset freezes and other controls. The final pages begin the Bolivia chapter with population estimates and discussion of social standing and community organizations.
